gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, according to Apple's own spec pages, the base M3 MacBook Air and the base 14-inch M3 MacBook Pro natively drive only one external display while the lid is open (a second one needs the lid closed, which defeats a laptop-plus-two-screens triple setup), that the MacBook Neo is limited to one external display even with the lid closed, and that the M4 MacBook Air is the first base Air that natively drives two external displays alongside its open built-in screen.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages uperfect.com/blogs/portable-monitor/best-triple-screen-laptop-extenders, rottenwifi.com/11-best-triple-portable-monitors-for-working-from-home-2026 and sekin.in/11-best-triple-portable-monitors-to-improve-your-productivity-while-wfh. UPERFECT says only that base M1 and M2 MacBooks support one external display and says nothing about M3, M4 or MacBook Neo. Rottenwifi and Sekin quote an Amazon Synnov listing that excludes M1/M2/M3 and say the Xebec Mac adapter is 'sold separately', but neither says which Macs need it. Sekin says Mobile Pixels 'documents multiple connection arrangements, including driver-based configurations' without giving the conditions. None of the three mentions the M3 lid-closed rule, the MacBook Neo limit, Xebec's 'all Mac users' adapter rule, or that the Trio 3 Pro needs software plus a power adapter to run from one cable. ChatGPT's own answer gave only the vague warning 'some MacBooks cannot drive two independent external displays natively'.
decides: The pick changes for Mac owners. On a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook, or a MacBook Neo, a 'driver-free, no-adapter' triple extender extends to only one side screen with the lid open. The shopper needs DisplayLink-type software (Trio 3 Pro: free software plus a power adapter for a single cable, per Macworld) or Xebec's Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter, which Xebec says every Mac user needs. On M4/M5 and Pro/Max Macs, the Trio 3 Pro works natively over two USB-C cables, which keeps it as the best overall pick. For Xebec, the separate adapter has to be added to the $699 price for any Mac.

findings.label: Native external displays with the built-in display on
findings.value: 1 external display (up to 6K 60 Hz); a second external display (up to 5K 60 Hz) only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Display Support section, M3 heading: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz' / 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display'. With the lid closed, the laptop's own screen is off, so this is not a laptop-plus-two-screens setup without extra software.

findings.label: Native external displays, base M3 chip
findings.value: 1 external display (up to 6K 60 Hz); a second (up to 5K 60 Hz) only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (14-inch, M3, Nov 2023) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Quoted from the Display Support section. The page I opened lists only the M3 chip, not M3 Pro or M3 Max.

findings.label: Native external displays
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays, up to 6K 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: No lid-closed condition is stated, so two side screens plus the open built-in display are supported natively.

findings.label: Native external displays
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 4K (3840 × 2160) 60 Hz, from the left-side USB-C port only; closing the lid does not add a second
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Neo - Apple Support
findings.note: Quotes: 'MacBook Neo supports one external display in addition to the built-in display.' 'Closing the lid of your MacBook Neo will not increase the number of external displays that can be supported.'

findings.label: Mac compatibility and cabling
findings.value: Base M1/M2 Macs and MacBook Neo need free DisplayLink-like software; Macs at or above a standard M1/M2/M3, including M1–M3 Pro/Max and all M4/M5, run both screens without software over 2 USB-C cables; a single-cable setup needs the software plus a power adapter on the Trio; up to 65 W pass-through
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review: MacBook's dual QHD screen wingspan (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Simon Jary at Macworld quotes the manual: no driver is needed if the laptop has 'two DP enabled USB-C ports'. Jary says the Trio cannot draw enough power from the laptop for maximum brightness without an adapter. His wording 'as or more powerful than a standard M1/M2/M3 processor' conflicts with Apple's M3 specs above, which allow only one external display with the lid open, so base-M3 owners should count on needing the software.

findings.label: Mac adapter requirement and port rules
findings.value: All Mac users need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter. On non-Mac laptops, USB-C ports labelled DisplayPort, DP Alt Mode or Thunderbolt 3+ need no adapter; ports labelled only 'USB-C, USB 3.2, or Gen 1' need the adapter; USB-A-only laptops need a USB-A to USB-C converter plus the adapter. Fits laptops from 13 to 18 inches.
findings.source_title: What laptops work with the Tri-Screen 3? - Xebec Help Center
findings.note: Maker help page, marked 'Updated a month ago'. Quote: 'All Mac users need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter.' Surface Pro setups are referred to a separate article.
